newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: US says still "far apart" in Japan insurance talks.
newsitem.headline: US says still "far apart" in Japan insurance talks.

text.p: Japan and the United States remain remain "very far apart" in negotiations to reach an agreement on liberalising Japan's insurance market, Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Monday.
"I believe we remain very far apart," Barshefsky told a news conference at the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) first ministerial conference in Singapore.
The United States and Japan have been intensely negotiating since last week to resolve their dispute over insurance liberalisation before a self-imposed December 15 deadline.

Barshefsky said U.S. negotiator Ira Shapiro would be coming to Singapore from Tokyo later on Monday, and she would decide sometime later whether to return to Tokyo herself after the WTO meeting ends on Friday for further talks.
"I would say that going back to Tokyo does frankly not necessarily indicate either that we think there will be an agreement or that there won't."
The disagreement between the two nations centres on U.S. charges that Japan is planning to renege on a 1994 trade agreement on the deregulation of its lucrative insurance market.

Washington has argued that the agreement calls for Tokyo to deregulate the huge primary life and casualty insurance sector, which is dominated by Japanese companies, before unleashing competition in the tiny specialty insurance market.
The niche market is the only one in which foreign insurance groups have a firm foothold.

Barshefsky's comments, on the sidelines of the World Trade Organisation's ministerial conference in Singapore, were in line with what a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official told reporters in Tokyo earlier on Monday.
Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said Japan wants the United States to be more flexible in negotiations on their bilateral insurance dispute.
If Barshefsky returns to Tokyo, she will meet Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka on Saturday to discuss the issue before the Sunday deadline.
"Japanese and U.S. negotiators are determined to reach an agreement by the deadline. We want to see further flexibility on the part of the U.S.," Ogawa said.
The two countries have been at odds over deregulation of Japan's domestic insurance market. and:

Separately, a Japanese finance ministry official said Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, and USTR negotiator Ira Shapiro will meet again on Thursday and Friday.
Sakakibara and Shapiro held two days of talks on Sunday and Monday after Mitsuzuka and Barshefsky failed to bridge their differences.
"We have deepened our understanding of each other's position, but differences that the ministers could not narrow in their latest talks still exist," the official said.
"Negotiations are going to be very hard," he said.

The MOF official said Japan has made "drastic" proposals to liberalise its primary life and casualty insurance sector, based on the spirit of the "Big Bang" financial reforms to implement substantial deregulation by 2001, mapped out by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto recently.
